content.text: I took a look at this one, but I'm not seeing the problem.  I recommend that unless it can clearly be reproduced we close it.
: in your local installation, do you see the "down arrow" within the green "Download Content" button? See comparison images above.
The problem is not apparent using ```mvn jetty:run``` but it is apparent in my local tomcat installation.

See attached screenshots of the glyphicon file's response headers.  Notice that jetty has no content-type and the content-length is just over half the size of what is reported by tomcat.  Tomcat on the other hand is returning the correct content-type.  Tomcat also reports console warning.  When I suppress the content-type in tomcat by commenting out the appropriate mimetypes in the global web.xml file,  I see the above warnings disappear but the icons still do not display.  It is also worth noting that the content-length doesn't change either.
I was not able to dig up anything useful searching for the console messages and other related queries. ("tomcat woff icons not displaying", etc)
My guess is that there is some kind of encoding or compression related issue.  Hmmm...
Maven filtering (resources plugin / war plugin) corrupts binary files. Some of the common image extensions are excluded by default and we can configure a list of file extensions to be excluded.
I have not explored in which version this bug was introduced, but the download  icon/image for binary content is no longer rendering.
See attached image for how the button currently looks.

Danny Bernstein: in your local installation, do you see the "down arrow" within the green "Download Content" button? See comparison images above.

The problem is not apparent using ```mvn jetty:run``` but it is apparent in my local tomcat installation.

See attached screenshots of the glyphicon file's response headers.  Notice that jetty has no content-type and the content-length is just over half the size of what is reported by tomcat.  Tomcat on the other hand is returning the correct content-type.  Tomcat also reports console warning.  When I suppress the content-type in tomcat by commenting out the appropriate mimetypes in the global web.xml file,  I see the above warnings disappear but the icons still do not display.  It is also worth noting that the content-length doesn't change either. 

I was not able to dig up anything useful searching for the console messages and other related queries. ("tomcat woff icons not displaying", etc)
My guess is that there is some kind of encoding or compression related issue.  Hmmm...

Maven filtering (resources plugin / war plugin) corrupts binary files. Some of the common image extensions are excluded by default and we can configure a list of file extensions to be excluded.

  • https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32690418/i-cant-load-fonts-while-using-tomcat
  • https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-resources-plugin/examples/binaries-filtering.html
  • https://maven.apache.org/plugins/maven-war-plugin/examples/adding-filtering-webresources.html

Fixed with PR: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1419
